newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says new highway concession plan soon.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says new highway concession plan soon.

text.p: Mexico's Transport Ministry (SCT) will give details of a new and less risky highway concession plan in the coming weeks, the Transport Minister said on Tuesday.

"The highway concession scheme will reduce risks for both the government and companies operating highways and I expect we shall announce it in the coming weeks," Transport Minister Carlos Ruiz Sacristan told journalists.
Ruiz declined to say what the government's stake would be in the new scheme.

Nonetheless, appendices to President Ernesto Zedillo's 1996 state of the nation speech reported that 14 billion pesos are earmarked for refinancing existing highway concession schemes and financing new ones to the year 2000.
Previously, Mexico has handed out concessions of 25 years to build and operate highways with the concession holder allowed to charge for its use.

Charges were subject to government approvals and the system has been besieged with problems largely because certain routes have not lived up to the traffic densities required by concession holders to be profitable.
-- Maria Luisa Aguilar, Mexico City bureau +525 728-9553
